overview: This Senate resolution supports naming the first week of August 2026 National Community Health Center Week. Community health centers are locally run nonprofit clinics, partly funded by the federal government, that provide primary care along with services like dental, mental health and pharmacy care, often in rural and low-income areas where other care is hard to find; the resolution says they serve up to 52 million people. It honors the centers' staff, board members and patients, celebrates their role over six decades, and encourages people to visit their local center. It does not change any law or provide money. The Senate approved it on August 7, 2026.
for: Supporters say community health centers are often the only nearby source of affordable care for millions of people, and recognizing them highlights their role in keeping communities healthy.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and offers praise without addressing the centers' long-term funding.
